en.cta.desc: Create a game, build a tool or explore neural simulation. Infernux is open source under MIT, with a public roadmap and a community shaping its next steps.
en.cta.title: Bring your world to Infernux.

en.footer.tagline: A Python-first game engine on the road to a Neural Network-Native Engine. Open source under MIT.
en.hero.subtitle: Python for gameplay, tools and computation. C++ for the runtime. Vulkan and WebGPU for your worlds.
en.home.capabilities.ai.body: Package components, tools and assets as .inxpkg. Runtime and Editor roles keep shipped code separate from authoring services. Add localized panels and menus, or use the optional MCP plugin to automate editor operations.
en.home.capabilities.ai.title: InxPackage plugins and MCP
en.home.capabilities.animation.body: 2D clips and sprite playback, embedded or separate FBX takes, skeletal animation, skinned meshes, state-machine graphs, and Timeline. Matching FBX joints map exactly, with importer pivot helpers handled and incompatible rigs rejected.
en.home.capabilities.animation.title: 2D and 3D animation
en.home.capabilities.asset.body: Project and package assets share GUID identities and live refresh. Player content stays in Content.inxpkg instead of exposing the authoring directory tree. Engine asset APIs resolve paths through the cooked index, with filesystem access for payloads that need it.
en.home.capabilities.asset.title: Assets and project pipeline
en.home.capabilities.data.body: Read and write world properties in batches through NumPy arrays. CPU/GPU JIT and Taichi integration let project scripts run numerical workloads, with target preparation and reusable warmup results.
en.home.capabilities.data.title: World data meets computation
en.home.capabilities.editor.body: Work across Scene/Game views, Hierarchy, Inspector, Project, Console, UI, animation and graph tools. Add your own dockable panels and nested menus while using the shared selection, commands and undo workflow.
en.home.capabilities.editor.title: An editor you can extend
en.home.capabilities.intro: Build on Python gameplay, native rendering and physics, imported content and extensible tools. The 041 development line deepens multi-scene editing, compute, world UI and live plugin authoring.
en.home.capabilities.physics.body: Jolt. Rigid bodies, colliders, scene queries, collision callbacks, layer filtering, transforms kept in sync with the scene. Its job system runs on the engine's own thread pool rather than spawning threads of its own.
en.home.capabilities.physics.title: Jolt physics
en.home.capabilities.render.body: Native Players use Vulkan; browser Players use WebGPU. Python defines the RenderStack and C++ runs the render graph. Shared scene and material data feed platform rendering, including lighting, shadows, UI, and particles.
en.home.capabilities.render.title: Vulkan and WebGPU
en.home.capabilities.script.body: Python components, Inspector fields, coroutines and prefabs support everyday gameplay. Transactional reload refreshes project and plugin components, including behavior on existing instances.
en.home.capabilities.script.title: Python gameplay layer
en.home.capabilities.title: From an idea to an interactive world.
en.home.capabilities.vfx.body: GPU Particle Graph: an emitter plus Init, Update and Rendering stages. The typed graph compiles to runtime IR ahead of time, outputs sprites or meshes, and previews in the editor with parameters you can drag while it runs.
en.home.capabilities.vfx.title: Particle Graph on the GPU
en.home.demo.intro: Not an offline render and not a concept image. Those blocks are ordinary GameObjects going through the ordinary Scene and Hierarchy, with no dedicated batching path. The tilt-shift, fog and colour on top are a RenderStack written in Python.
en.home.demo.panel.item1: 65,536 standard GameObjects sharing one mesh and one material. You can still select them in the Hierarchy and edit them. They are no different from a cube you dropped in by hand.
en.home.demo.panel.item2: Tilt-shift focus, distance fog, height fog, colour controls and MSAA all come from one custom RenderStack. Change it in the editor and you see the result immediately.
en.home.demo.panel.item3: The raw editor capture. Nothing retouched.
en.home.demo.title: A voxel continent of 65,536 objects, built in the editor and rendered in the editor.
en.home.hero.description: Create games with Python, a C++ runtime and Vulkan / WebGPU rendering. Infernux connects scenes, simulation, compute and extensible tools today, with a roadmap toward worlds that neural networks can observe, learn from and act within.
en.home.hero.kicker: MIT · open source · built around Python
en.home.hero.platform: Editors: Windows / Linux · Players: Windows / Linux / Android / Web · 0.4.1
en.home.hero.title:
Build worlds.
Give them intelligence.
en.home.manifesto: Neural Network-Native Engine (3N) is our destination: models should work with world data and simulation as part of the engine. Python, batch APIs and CPU/GPU compute form the foundation; portable inference, replay and the full tensor data plane are next.
en.home.status.card1.body: Start with Windows and Linux Editors, Windows/Linux/Android/Web Players, InxPackage assets and Hub-managed environments. Check the download page for available release artifacts.
en.home.status.card1.title: Four platforms, packed assets, plugins
en.home.status.card2.body: Multi-scene editing, model import, CPU/GPU JIT, physics queries and world UI grow alongside plugin hot reload, Player type registration and platform-specific build settings. Read the branch changelog for the full scope.
en.home.status.card2.title: Worlds, compute and live tools
en.home.status.intro: Published downloads and the active development line are tracked separately. The roadmap describes the further work toward a complete 3N workflow.
en.home.status.title: Build today. Follow what comes next.
en.home.system.card1.body: Import content, assemble scenes, tune behavior and export a Player. Rendering, resources, physics and tools work together around the game you are making.
en.home.system.card1.title: 1 · A complete game workflow
en.home.system.card2.body: Use Python for gameplay, editor extensions, render authoring and computation. C++ and the GPU handle the performance-critical runtime work behind those interfaces.
en.home.system.card2.title: 2 · Python authors, C++ executes
en.home.system.card3.body: GUID asset identities, editor commands and transactional reload make changes traceable. The optional MCP plugin lets agents use the editor command and undo paths, with inspectable results.
en.home.system.card3.title: 3 · Explicit, observable operations
en.home.system.intro: A clear division of work keeps everyday iteration fast and ambitious systems understandable.
en.home.system.title: Built for authors. Open to inspection.
en.home.thesis.card1.body: Scenes, materials, animation, physics, audio and UI turn an idea into an interactive world. Python lets gameplay and custom tools grow together as your project takes shape.
en.home.thesis.card1.title: Start with a world worth playing
en.home.thesis.card2.body: Batch APIs expose world state to Python. CPU/GPU JIT and Taichi integration support computational gameplay. These are foundations for richer model interaction with the world.
en.home.thesis.card2.title: Bring computation into the simulation
en.home.thesis.card3.body: The next stages connect model workflows, portable inference, replay and batch environments. The destination is a repeatable route from experimentation to a model-powered game on the target device.
en.home.thesis.card3.title: Make neural systems part of the game
en.home.thesis.intro: A neural-native engine connects the game you build to the data a model needs. Infernux is developing that connection from world representation through simulation and tools to deployment.
en.home.thesis.title: A playable world. A learning environment. One engine.
en.roadmap.hero.description: Our destination is a Neural Network-Native Engine (3N). This roadmap connects world authoring to model workflows, inference, replay and batch simulation; the 041 line strengthens the engine foundation.
en.roadmap.hero.title: Infernux roadmap
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.item1: One project exporting an Android APK/AAB and a Web package you can deploy as it is.
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.item2: A Linux Player, plus windowless and offscreen runs for CI, servers and large-scale simulation.
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.item3: Platform capabilities declared up front, and missing ones failing loudly. No silent downgrades; quiet fallback is a debugging nightmare.
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.title: Shipping
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.item1: Standard PyTorch right in the editor: develop, train, evaluate and export without switching environments.
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.item2: A Player that carries only the inference runtime its platform needs. No CUDA Toolkit, no entire training stack riding along.
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.item3: Every hop between Torch, DLPack and GPU buffers measured, and every copy written down in the docs.
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.title: Model data
en.roadmap.lanes.card3.item1: Versioned reflection plus Command/Query schemas, so UI, Python and MCP read one definition instead of each reimplementing it.
en.roadmap.lanes.card3.item2: World snapshot and delta, deterministic replay contracts, and batched create, step and reset.
en.roadmap.lanes.card3.title: Semantic world
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.item1: An Engine Tool ships with its schema, permissions, tests, provenance, resource limits and lifecycle attached.
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.item2: Plugins and models get a real distribution format, and their own tests run in a sandbox before anything enters your project.
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.item3: Anything an agent builds clears the same bar as human-written code before it goes near someone else's project.
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.title: Tools and ecosystem
en.roadmap.lanes.intro: They share their plumbing. Platform contracts decide where a Player can run. Schemas decide who is allowed to change the world. Replay serves debugging and training equally well. Tool governance covers plugins and agents with the same machinery.
en.roadmap.lanes.title: Four tracks, and they all have to end up in one engine.
en.roadmap.priorities.card1.body: Define shared schemas for state, commands and queries, building on the existing editor command path and batch APIs. Tools and models should be able to discover exactly what they can read and change.
en.roadmap.priorities.card1.title: A shared language for world state
en.roadmap.priorities.card2.body: Develop snapshot, delta and replay contracts, then batch stepping and tensor exchange. Make copying, synchronization and ownership explicit so workloads can be measured and improved.
en.roadmap.priorities.card2.title: Repeatable simulation and data exchange
en.roadmap.priorities.card3.body: Keep the Python ML ecosystem close to authoring. Choose deployment backends using model coverage, latency, memory and package size on each target, and ship only the runtime the game needs.
en.roadmap.priorities.card3.title: Model workflows and portable inference
en.roadmap.priorities.intro: Four-platform exports are in place. Further work focuses on compute boundaries, repeatable world operations and model deployment across those targets.
en.roadmap.priorities.title: Connect models, worlds and deployment.
en.roadmap.release.current.item1: The 041 development line deepens multi-scene editing, model import and source synchronization, world UI, CPU/GPU JIT preparation and physics queries.
en.roadmap.release.current.item2: Plugin components share live reload with project scripts. Player type registration, preload cleanup, localization and platform build options make extensions part of the everyday workflow.
en.roadmap.release.current.title: Multi-scene worlds and live tools
en.roadmap.release.long.item1: 0.5.0 formalises Engine Tools and draws a hard line between trusted and untrusted execution. 0.5.1 ships the distribution format for plugins and models, with their own tests run in a sandbox before anything lands in your project.
en.roadmap.release.long.item2: 0.5.2 has to string cross-platform Players, models, schemas, replay, batch worlds and tool governance into one path somebody can walk end to end, live.
en.roadmap.release.long.title: Tools an agent can build, on an engine that holds together
en.roadmap.release.mid.item1: 041 establishes the cross-platform runtime and authoring foundation. The planned 0.4.2–0.4.4 stages focus on shared schemas, snapshots and replay, then batch worlds and the tensor data plane.
en.roadmap.release.mid.item2: Each stage needs usable public APIs and measurable behavior so games, tools and model workflows can build on the same contracts.
en.roadmap.release.mid.title: Headless, semantics, replay, batch data
en.roadmap.release.next.item1: 0.4.1 brings larger worlds, live Python authoring and target-aware computation into the same engine workflow. This release expands multi-scene editing, prefab authoring, model import, rendering and audio, then carries their resource and component lifecycles into exported Players. It also rebuilds key parts of the plugin experience in response to community reports.
en.roadmap.release.next.item2: Read the Changelog for features, fixes, platform boundaries and upgrade notes.
en.roadmap.release.next.title: Worlds, Compute and Live Tools

en.roadmap.orbit.caption: Select a node by click, tap or keyboard. Arrows connect foundations to the capabilities they support.

zh.footer.tagline: 以 Python 为主要创作语言，致力于成为 Neural Network-Native Engine。MIT 开源。
zh.hero.subtitle: Python 编写玩法、工具与计算，C++ 承担运行时，Vulkan 与 WebGPU 呈现你的世界。
zh.home.capabilities.ai.body: 将组件、工具与资产打包成 .inxpkg。Runtime 与 Editor 角色明确区分发布代码与创作服务。添加本地化面板和菜单，也可以使用可选 MCP 插件自动化编辑器操作。
zh.home.capabilities.ai.title: InxPackage 插件与 MCP
zh.home.capabilities.animation.body: 2D Clip 与序列帧、FBX 内嵌或独立动画、骨骼动画、蒙皮网格、状态机图与 Timeline。精确映射匹配的 FBX 关节，处理导入器 pivot 辅助节点，并明确拒绝不兼容骨架。
zh.home.capabilities.animation.title: 2D / 3D 动画
zh.home.capabilities.asset.body: 项目和插件资产共用 GUID 身份与实时刷新流程。Player 内容保留在 Content.inxpkg 中，不再展开创作目录树。引擎资产 API 通过构建索引解析路径，需要真实文件的载荷也能获得文件系统访问。
zh.home.capabilities.asset.title: 资产与项目管线
zh.home.capabilities.data.body: 通过 NumPy 数组批量读写世界属性。CPU/GPU JIT 与 Taichi 集成让项目脚本执行数值计算，并结合目标平台准备与可复用预热结果。
zh.home.capabilities.data.title: 世界数据与计算相连
zh.home.capabilities.editor.body: 在 Scene/Game、Hierarchy、Inspector、Project、Console、UI、动画和图工具间协作。添加自己的可停靠面板与多级菜单，沿用统一的选择、命令与撤销流程。
zh.home.capabilities.editor.title: 可以扩展的编辑器
zh.home.capabilities.intro: 以 Python 玩法、原生渲染与物理、导入资源和可扩展工具构建游戏。041 开发主线进一步完善多场景编辑、计算、世界 UI 与插件实时创作。
zh.home.capabilities.physics.body: Jolt。刚体、碰撞体、场景查询、碰撞回调、层过滤，变换和场景保持同步。它的作业系统接在引擎自己的线程池上，不会另开一堆线程。
zh.home.capabilities.physics.title: Jolt 物理
zh.home.capabilities.render.body: 原生 Player 使用 Vulkan，浏览器 Player 使用 WebGPU。Python 定义 RenderStack，C++ 执行渲染图。共享场景与材质数据用于各平台渲染，覆盖光照、阴影、UI 和粒子。
zh.home.capabilities.render.title: Vulkan 与 WebGPU
zh.home.capabilities.script.body: Python 组件、Inspector 字段、协程与 Prefab 支持日常玩法开发。事务式重载刷新项目和插件组件，包括已有实例的行为。
zh.home.capabilities.script.title: Python 玩法层
zh.home.capabilities.title: 从想法，到可以交互的世界。
zh.home.capabilities.vfx.body: GPU Particle Graph：一个发射器加 Init / Update / Rendering 三段。类型化的图提前编译成运行时 IR，Sprite 和 Mesh 都能出，编辑器里能预览，参数能一边跑一边拖。
zh.home.capabilities.vfx.title: 跑在 GPU 上的 Particle Graph
zh.home.demo.intro: 不是离线渲染，也不是概念图。这些方块是普通 GameObject，走的是普通的 Scene 和 Hierarchy，没有专门的批渲染通道。上面那层移轴、雾和色彩，是一条用 Python 写出来的 RenderStack。
zh.home.demo.panel.item1: 65,536 个标准 GameObject 共享一套网格和材质。它们在 Hierarchy 里照样能选中、能改，和你手动放进去的那个方块没有任何区别。
zh.home.demo.panel.item2: 移轴对焦、距离雾、高度雾、色彩控制、MSAA，全部来自同一条自定义 RenderStack。在编辑器里改完，当场就能看到结果。
zh.home.demo.panel.item3: 技术展示的原始截图，1920 × 1032，没做后期。
zh.home.demo.title: 65,536 个物体的体素大陆，在编辑器里搭的，也在编辑器里渲的。
zh.home.hero.description: 用 Python、C++ 运行时和 Vulkan / WebGPU 创造游戏。今天的熔炉连接场景、模拟、计算与可扩展工具；沿着路线图，让神经网络能够观察世界、从中学习并参与其中。
zh.home.hero.kicker: MIT 开源 · 以 Python 为主要创作语言
zh.home.hero.platform: 编辑器：Windows / Linux · Player：Windows / Linux / Android / Web · 0.4.1
zh.home.hero.title:
创造世界，
让智能成为其中一部分。
zh.home.manifesto: 我们致力于成为 Neural Network-Native Engine（3N），即神经网络原生引擎：让模型通过引擎直接参与世界数据与模拟。Python、批量 API 和 CPU/GPU 计算构成基础，可移植推理、回放与完整张量数据面是后续方向。
zh.home.status.card1.body: 从 Windows/Linux 编辑器、四端 Player、InxPackage 资源与 Hub 托管环境开始。可用发行包以下载页为准。
zh.home.status.card1.title: 四端发布、资源封包与插件
zh.home.status.card2.body: 多场景编辑、模型导入、CPU/GPU JIT、物理查询与世界 UI，结合插件热重载、Player 类型注册和各平台构建选项。完整范围见分支更新日志。
zh.home.status.card2.title: 世界、计算与实时工具
zh.home.status.intro: 公开下载与当前开发主线分别记录。路线图说明了走向完整 3N 工作流还需要完成的阶段。
zh.home.status.title: 现在开始创作，关注接下来的进展。
zh.home.system.card1.body: 导入内容、组织场景、调整行为、导出 Player。渲染、资源、物理与工具围绕你正在制作的游戏共同工作。
zh.home.system.card1.title: 1 · 完整的游戏工作流
zh.home.system.card2.body: 用 Python 编写玩法、编辑器扩展、渲染编排和计算，由 C++ 与 GPU 承担接口背后对性能敏感的运行时工作。
zh.home.system.card2.title: 2 · Python 创作，C++ 执行
zh.home.system.card3.body: GUID 资源身份、编辑器命令与事务式重载让修改可追踪。可选 MCP 插件让 Agent 使用编辑器的命令和撤销路径，并检查实际结果。
zh.home.system.card3.title: 3 · 明确、可观察的操作
zh.home.system.intro: 清晰的职责划分，让日常迭代顺畅，也让复杂系统有据可查。
zh.home.system.title: 服务创作，也经得起检查。
zh.home.thesis.card1.body: 场景、材质、动画、物理、音频与 UI 把想法变成可以交互的世界。随着项目成形，用 Python 让玩法和专属工具一起成长。
zh.home.thesis.card1.title: 先创造值得游玩的世界
zh.home.thesis.card2.body: 批量 API 向 Python 开放世界状态，CPU/GPU JIT 与 Taichi 集成支持计算驱动的玩法，为模型与世界的进一步交互建立基础。
zh.home.thesis.card2.title: 让计算参与模拟
zh.home.thesis.card3.body: 后续阶段连接模型工作流、可移植推理、回放与批量环境，让实验走向目标设备上的实际游戏，并让这个过程可以重复。
zh.home.thesis.card3.title: 让神经系统成为游戏的一部分
zh.home.thesis.intro: 神经网络原生引擎连接你创造的游戏与模型需要的数据。熔炉从世界表示出发，将模拟、工具与部署逐步连成一条工作流。
zh.home.thesis.title: 可游玩的世界，也是智能学习和行动的环境。

zh.roadmap.hero.description: 我们致力于成为 Neural Network-Native Engine（3N），即神经网络原生引擎。路线图将世界创作连接到模型工作流、推理、回放与批量模拟；041 继续完善引擎基础。
zh.roadmap.hero.title: 熔炉路线图
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.item1: 同一个项目导出 Android APK/AAB，也导出能直接部署的 Web 包体。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.item2: Linux Player，以及给 CI、服务器和大规模仿真用的无窗口、离屏运行。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.item3: 平台能力提前声明，缺什么直接报错。绝不悄悄降级——静默 fallback 是调试地狱。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.title: 发布
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.item1: 编辑器里就是标准 PyTorch，开发、训练、评估、导出都不用换环境。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.item2: Player 只带目标平台用得上的推理运行时，不塞 CUDA Toolkit，也不背整个训练栈。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.item3: Torch、DLPack、GPU buffer 之间每一跳都测过，每一次拷贝都写进文档。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.title: 模型数据
zh.roadmap.lanes.card3.item1: 版本化反射加 Command/Query schema，UI、Python、MCP 读同一份定义，不再各写一遍。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card3.item2: 世界 snapshot 与 delta、确定性回放契约，以及批量的 create、step、reset。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card3.title: 语义世界
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.item1: Engine Tool 出厂就带着 schema、权限、测试、来源、资源上限和生命周期。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.item2: 插件和模型有正式的分发格式，进你的项目之前先在沙箱里跑完它自带的测试。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.item3: Agent 造出来的东西想进别人的项目，要过和人写的代码一样的关。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.title: 工具与生态
zh.roadmap.lanes.intro: 四条线共用同一批地基：平台契约决定 Player 能跑在哪，schema 决定谁能改世界，回放同时服务调试和训练，工具治理用同一套机制管住插件和 Agent。
zh.roadmap.lanes.title: 四条线，最后得拧成一台引擎。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card1.body: 在现有编辑器命令路径与批量 API 上建立统一的状态、命令和查询 Schema，让工具与模型准确发现可读取和修改的内容。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card1.title: 统一描述世界状态
zh.roadmap.priorities.card2.body: 建设快照、增量与回放契约，进一步推进批量步进和张量交换。明确复制、同步与所有权，让任务可以测量和优化。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card2.title: 可重复模拟与数据交换
zh.roadmap.priorities.card3.body: 让 Python 机器学习生态靠近创作流程，根据各目标的模型覆盖率、延迟、内存和包体选择部署后端，只分发游戏需要的运行时。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card3.title: 模型工作流与可移植推理
zh.roadmap.priorities.intro: 四端导出已经建立，后续聚焦计算边界、可重复的世界操作，以及跨目标平台的模型部署。
zh.roadmap.priorities.title: 连接模型、世界与部署。
zh.roadmap.release.current.item1: 041 开发主线完善多场景编辑、模型导入与源同步、世界 UI、CPU/GPU JIT 准备和物理查询。
zh.roadmap.release.current.item2: 插件组件与项目脚本共享实时重载。Player 类型注册、preload 清理、本地化与平台构建选项让扩展融入日常开发。
zh.roadmap.release.current.title: 多场景世界与实时工具
zh.roadmap.release.long.item1: 0.5.0 把 Engine Tool 正式化，在可信和不可信执行之间划一条死线。0.5.1 交付插件和模型的分发格式，装进项目之前先在沙箱里跑完它自带的测试。
zh.roadmap.release.long.item2: 0.5.2 要把跨平台 Player、模型、schema、回放、批量世界和工具治理串成一条能当场从头走到尾的路径。
zh.roadmap.release.long.title: Agent 造得出的工具，和一台合得上的引擎
zh.roadmap.release.mid.item1: 041 建立跨平台运行时与创作基础。规划中的 0.4.2–0.4.4 依次推进统一 Schema、快照与回放，再到批量世界和张量数据面。
zh.roadmap.release.mid.item2: 每个阶段都需要可用的公开 API 与可测量的行为，让游戏、工具和模型工作流建立在同一套契约之上。
zh.roadmap.release.mid.title: 无窗口、语义、回放、批量数据
zh.roadmap.release.next.item1: 0.4.1 把更大的世界、实时 Python 创作与面向目标平台的计算带进同一套引擎工作流。本期扩展了多场景、Prefab、模型导入、渲染和音频能力，并把资源与组件的生命周期贯通到导出的 Player；同时根据社区反馈，完善了插件开发和热重载的关键环节。
zh.roadmap.release.next.item2: 详细能力、问题修复、平台边界与升级须知请查看更新日志。
zh.roadmap.release.next.title: 世界、计算与实时创作工具
